text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered: P1 network degradation in azure-koreasouth affecting Private deployments' egress to on-prem. Multiple customer reports of 502s / high tail latency. Auto-escalation to SRE and NetEng.

mike_sre: I'm on it. Observing elevated TCP retransmits on our egress gateways in koreasouth. Packet loss ~4-6% to the on-prem edge.

sam_neteng: Seeing BGP session flaps on a subset of Azure peering links. Routes are oscillating between two backbones; next-hop path changes every ~30s.

lia_product: Customers reporting API errors and model timeouts. Liaising with two enterprise customers (CorpA, FinX) on standby.

anne_support: CorpA says degraded since ~10m ago, they see token generation failures and retry storms on our client. They've opened an internal incident.

pagerduty: @mike_sre, you were the on-call for infra. Please acknowledge.

mike_sre: acknowledged. I'll grab BGP dumps and health metrics.

sam_neteng: Pasted snippet of BGP shows repeated withdrawal/announce cycles for the egress prefix:```
# bgp show
Prefix: 203.0.113.0/24
Path: 65000 65100 65200
Attr: MED changed, next-hop flip
Counts: withdraw/announce x 14
```

mike_sre: Correlating with our telemetry, the KV cache hit rate dropped and we see increased cold starts for large-context requests. Likely due to requests being re-routed through a higher-latency path and timing out to fallback.

sam_neteng: Azure status feed (scraped): "Networking teams investigating intermittent egress route instability in koreasouth region affecting ExpressRoute/Private Peering." No ETA.

azure-status-bot: Azure advisory link: https://status.azure.com/incident/XXXXXX - currently labeled "Investigating".

lia_product: Impact: Hosted API OK, but customers on Private (VPC/on-prem) using Dedicated egress through koreasouth are impacted. Estimate ~8 active customers; 3 reporting visible errors. Severity P1 for impacted customers.

mike_sre: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) Route policy fallback -> prefer alternate private region (koreacentral) for affected customer prefixes via smart-routing. 2) Temporarily enable client-side retry/backoff bump in edge proxies. 3) Engage Azure TAC for BGP stabilization.

sam_neteng: I can push a selective route preference change for the affected prefixes now. Will annotate with runbook id: RB-203-az-egress-failover.

anne_support: I'll notify CorpA and FinX: planned automatic reroute to koreacentral; we'll monitor application-level errors and ask them to throttle retries for 15m. Drafting message now.

lia_product: Any downstream risk to token accounting or billing from re-routing? We might incur cross-region egress cost but that's acceptable for P1 mitigation. Notify finance if prolonged.

mike_sre: Acknowledged. Tracking cost impact in incident doc.

sam_neteng: Executing route preference change:```
# route-policy apply
match community AFF-PRIVATE-203
set local-pref 200
commit
```

sam_neteng: Done. BGP update propagated. Observability: packet loss dropped from 5% -> 0.7% on affected path within 90s.

mike_sre: Confirming application metrics improving: 502s dropping, p95 latency trending down. KV cache warmed back within 3 minutes.

anne_support: CorpA acknowledged automatic reroute. They report their error rate falling. FinX still seeing intermittent spikes, asking for ETA.

lia_product: Can we add a temporary explicit fallback model routing rule so that customer requests that hit the flaky path get a fast fallback to hosted API for critical requests? Might reduce errors while we wait for Azure.

mike_sre: Yes—I'll flip the policy for affected customer IDs to prefer hosted endpoints for write-heavy routes. Doing it now.

mike_sre: Policy change applied. FinX reporting immediate improvement.

sam_neteng: Azure TAC engaged (case #987654). They confirm internal fabric maintenance contributing to transient route churn in koreasouth. They've opened an internal fix but no ETA.

anne_support: Logging customer communications. Preparing post-incident note and remediation checklist for customers with private egress.

lia_product: Action items captured: 1) Follow up with Azure TAC until stable. 2) Add more aggressive health-triggered route failover to our smart router (auto-detect >1% loss for 60s). 3) Postmortem with timeline and customer impact. 4) Notify Finance if cross-region egress > $X/day. 5) Run a chaos test to validate fallback behavior.

mike_sre: I'll own item 2 and the postmortem. Sam to own Azure TAC liaison and route policy logs. Anne to own customer comms. Lia to coordinate postmortem and product impact summary.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged and marked active. SLA window started.

incident-bot: Incident update logged: P1 - azure-koreasouth egress instability - mitigation (selective route failover & hosted fallback) applied. Next update in 30m or on significant change.

anne_support: Final note for handoff: @mike_sre I'm stepping out at 30m for another pager. Leaving monitoring to you and Sam. I'll update the customer thread with the mitigation steps.

mike_sre: Roger. I'll monitor and escalate if we see re-regression. Leaving this thread for on-call handoff later with full notes.

sam_neteng: Leaving BGP dumps and route policy diffs in /runbooks/incidents/2423501234. Will attach to the Azure TAC case.

lia_product: Thanks all. We'll reconvene for a 1hr postmortem after incident close.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed for public notifications; internal monitoring continues.
